# feature-management-sdk-proxy

Dynatrace Feature Management SDK Proxy, a caching and SSE fan-out egress point for Feature Management server SDKs

<!-- This file is generated by helm-docs from README.md.gotmpl and values.yaml. Run `make helm-docs`; don't edit README.md directly. -->

## Install

```bash
helm install sdk-proxy ./charts/feature-management-sdk-proxy --namespace sdk-proxy --create-namespace
```

Verify with `helm test sdk-proxy -n sdk-proxy`, which calls `/readyz` through the Service.

## SDK Setup

Set the server SDK's `configOrigin` to the Service URL. The SDK then fetches its config from
`<configOrigin>/server/<sdk_key>.json`, subscribes to `/sse` on the proxy, and posts evaluation metrics to
`<configOrigin>/v1/metrics`. The SDK key is passed through on every request; the proxy holds no credentials.

```text
http://<release>-feature-management-sdk-proxy.<namespace>.svc:8080
```

For example, with the Java provider:

```java
DynatraceProviderOptions options = DynatraceProviderOptions.builder()
    .configOrigin("http://sdk-proxy-feature-management-sdk-proxy.sdk-proxy.svc:8080")
    .build();
```

`helm install` prints the exact URL for your release.

## Required Egress

The proxy makes outbound HTTPS (443) connections only. The upstream hosts are derived from each SDK key's region
segment (`<geo>`) and `cdnBaseDomain` (default `fm.dynatrace.com`):

| Destination                  | Host                                                              | Used for                                                    |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Config CDN                   | `cdn.<geo>.<cdnBaseDomain>`                                       | Flag config fetches and background revalidation             |
| Metrics ingest               | `metrics.<geo>.<cdnBaseDomain>`                                   | `POST /v1/metrics` forwarding                               |
| Upstream SSE                 | Host of `eventStreamEndpoint` in the config                       | One change-notification stream per SDK key                  |
| Snapshot storage (optional)  | Provider endpoint for `snapshot.url`, or its `endpoint=` override | Snapshot reads and writes                                   |
| OTLP collector (optional)    | `otel.endpoint`                                                   | Metrics, traces, and logs export (often in-cluster on 4318) |
| Workload identity (optional) | Provider token endpoint                                           | Credentials for snapshot storage                            |

With `networkPolicy.enabled`, DNS and TCP 443 to any address except the cloud metadata service are allowed. Add
`networkPolicy.extraEgress` rules for anything else, such as an in-cluster OTel collector or the GKE metadata server:

```yaml
networkPolicy:
  enabled: true
  extraEgress:
    # GKE Workload Identity metadata server
    - to:
        - ipBlock:
            cidr: 169.254.169.252/32
      ports:
        - port: 988
          protocol: TCP
    # In-cluster OTel collector
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
      ports:
        - port: 4318
          protocol: TCP
  ingress:
    from:
      - namespaceSelector:
          matchLabels:
            kubernetes.io/metadata.name: apps
```

EKS IRSA and Azure Workload Identity exchange tokens with public HTTPS endpoints, which the default 443 rule covers.

## Snapshot Persistence

Snapshots let restarted and newly scheduled pods start warm from object storage instead of hitting the CDN for every
key. `snapshot.url` selects the backend: `s3://` (AWS S3 and S3-compatible stores), `gs://` (Google Cloud Storage),
`azblob://` (Azure Blob Storage), or `file://`. Credentials come from each provider's native credential chain, so
workload identity needs no static secrets.

EKS (IRSA):

```yaml
serviceAccount:
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sdk-proxy-snapshots
snapshot:
  enabled: true
  url: s3://my-proxy-snapshots?region=us-east-1&prefix=prod
```

GKE (Workload Identity):

```yaml
serviceAccount:
  annotations:
    iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: sdk-proxy@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
snapshot:
  enabled: true
  url: gs://my-proxy-snapshots?prefix=prod
```

AKS (Workload Identity):

```yaml
serviceAccount:
  annotations:
    azure.workload.identity/client-id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
podLabels:
  azure.workload.identity/use: "true"
snapshot:
  enabled: true
  url: azblob://my-proxy-snapshots?storage_account=myaccount&prefix=prod
```

Static credentials are passed as the provider's own environment variables. With an existing Secret whose keys are the
variable names (here `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`), loaded with `envFrom`:

```yaml
snapshot:
  enabled: true
  url: s3://my-proxy-snapshots?region=us-east-1&endpoint=http://minio.storage:9000&use_path_style=true
  credentials:
    existingSecret: sdk-proxy-snapshot-credentials
```

Or let the chart create the Secret from `snapshot.credentials.env`, e.g. `AZURE_STORAGE_KEY` for Azure shared keys.
GCS service-account key files aren't environment variables: mount the key with `extraVolumes`/`extraVolumeMounts` and
set `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` via `extraEnv`.

## What the Chart Configures

- `/livez` liveness, `/readyz` readiness, and a startup probe that holds off liveness checks during startup.
- `PROXY_INSTANCE_ID` set to the pod name, so usage records identify each replica.
- A 60s termination grace period, covering `shutdownTimeout` (30s) plus the SSE, snapshot, and usage flush steps.
- Non-root UID/GID 65532, read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`, and no
  ServiceAccount token mounted.
- A rolling update with `maxUnavailable: 0`, and a PodDisruptionBudget.
- Config and Secret checksums on the pod template, so changes roll the pods.

`values.schema.json` rejects unknown keys and invalid values, and the templates reject inconsistent snapshot settings
at render time instead of producing a pod that exits 1 at startup.

## Multiple Replicas

Each replica keeps its own cache and its own upstream SSE connection per SDK key. An SDK's config request and its
`/sse` subscription can land on different pods; if that pod hasn't cached the key yet, it answers `412` and the SDK
retries. Set `service.sessionAffinity: ClientIP` to pin clients to one pod, or enable snapshots so new pods start warm.

## Ingress

For SDKs outside the cluster, enable `ingress`. `/sse` is a long-lived Server-Sent Events stream, so turn off
response buffering and raise read timeouts. For ingress-nginx:

```yaml
ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: nginx
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffering: "off"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "3600"
  hosts:
    - host: sdk-proxy.example.com
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
```

| serviceAccount.automountServiceAccountToken | bool | `false` | Mount the ServiceAccount token. The proxy doesn't call the Kubernetes API; projected workload identity tokens are mounted separately by the provider's webhook. |
| serviceAccount.create | bool | `true` | Create a ServiceAccount. |
| serviceAccount.name | string | `""` | ServiceAccount name. Generated from the full name when empty. |
| shutdownTimeout | string | `"30s"` | Graceful shutdown drain timeout (`SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`). Keep `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` at least 20s above it. |
| snapshot.credentials.env | object | `{}` | Env var name to value; the chart creates a Secret loaded with `envFrom`. |
| snapshot.credentials.existingSecret | string | `""` | Existing Secret loaded with `envFrom`. |
| snapshot.enabled | bool | `false` | Enable snapshot persistence. |
| snapshot.maxAge | string | `nil` | Snapshots older than this are treated as stale at startup (`SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE`, proxy default 24h). |
| snapshot.url | string | `""` | Bucket URL (`SNAPSHOT_URL`), e.g. `s3://bucket?region=us-east-1`, `gs://bucket`, `azblob://container?storage_account=name`. Required when `snapshot.enabled`. |
| snapshot.writeQueueSize | string | `nil` | Async write queue size (`SNAPSHOT_WRITE_QUEUE_SIZE`, proxy default 256). |
| sse.enabled | bool | `true` | Enable SSE fan-out. `false` sets `SSE_DISABLED=true` (SDKs fall back to polling). |
| sse.fanoutCapPerKey | string | `nil` | Max downstream subscribers per SDK key (`SSE_FANOUT_CAP_PER_KEY`, proxy default 1000, 0 = unlimited). |
| sse.subscribeBurst | string | `nil` | Per-key subscribe burst (`SSE_SUBSCRIBE_BURST`, proxy default 100). |
| sse.subscribeRatePerSec | string | `nil` | Per-key subscribe rate limit (`SSE_SUBSCRIBE_RATE_PER_SEC`, proxy default 20). |
| startupProbe | object | `{"failureThreshold":30,"httpGet":{"path":"/livez","port":"http"},"periodSeconds":2}` | Startup probe, which holds off liveness checks during startup. |
| terminationGracePeriodSeconds | int | `60` | Pod termination grace period. Shutdown takes up to `shutdownTimeout` + 5s (SSE) + snapshot drain + 10s (usage flush); keep this above that sum. |
| tolerations | list | `[]` | Tolerations. |
| topologySpreadConstraints | list | `[]` | Topology spread constraints. Values are templated. |
